 import { defineSchema, defineTable } from "convex/server";
 import { v } from "convex/values";
 
 import { decisionValidator } from "../src/lib/decision";
 
 export default defineSchema({
   institutions: defineTable({
     name: v.string(),
     code: v.string(),
     createdAt: v.number(),
   }).index("by_code", ["code"]),
 
   users: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     email: v.string(),
     name: v.string(),
     usn: v.optional(v.string()),
     role: v.union(
       v.literal("student"),
       v.literal("faculty"),
       v.literal("department_authority"),
       v.literal("admin"),
       v.literal("auditor"),
     ),
     status: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("invited"), v.literal("active"), v.literal("suspended"))),
     createdAt: v.number(),
   })
     .index("by_institution", ["institutionId"])
     .index("by_email", ["email"])
     .index("by_institution_usn", ["institutionId", "usn"]),
 
   password_credentials: defineTable({
     userId: v.id("users"),
     hash: v.string(),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     updatedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   }).index("by_user", ["userId"]),
 
   password_login_attempts: defineTable({
     subjectKey: v.string(),
     institutionId: v.optional(v.id("institutions")),
     attempts: v.number(),
     windowStartAt: v.number(),
   }).index("by_subjectKey", ["subjectKey"]),
 
   courses: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     code: v.string(),
     title: v.string(),
     department: v.optional(v.string()),
   }).index("by_institution_code", ["institutionId", "code"]),
 
   sections: defineTable({
     courseId: v.id("courses"),
     name: v.string(),
     term: v.optional(v.string()),
   }).index("by_course", ["courseId"]),
 
   venues: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     name: v.string(),
     capacity: v.optional(v.number()),
     latitude: v.optional(v.number()),
     longitude: v.optional(v.number()),
     geofenceRadiusMeters: v.optional(v.number()),
   }).index("by_institution", ["institutionId"]),
 
   timetable_slots: defineTable({
     sectionId: v.id("sections"),
     venueId: v.id("venues"),
     dayOfWeek: v.number(),
     startMinutes: v.number(),
     endMinutes: v.number(),
     facultyId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
   })
     .index("by_section", ["sectionId"])
     .index("by_venue", ["venueId"])
     .index("by_faculty_day", ["facultyId", "dayOfWeek"]),
 
   enrollments: defineTable({
     studentId: v.id("users"),
     sectionId: v.id("sections"),
     enrolledAt: v.number(),
   })
     .index("by_student", ["studentId"])
     .index("by_section", ["sectionId"]),
 
   attendance_events: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     studentId: v.id("users"),
     sectionId: v.id("sections"),
     sessionId: v.optional(v.id("class_sessions")),
     state: v.union(
       v.literal("initiated"),
       v.literal("authenticated"),
       v.literal("session_verified"),
       v.literal("presence_evaluated"),
       v.literal("risk_evaluated"),
       v.literal("step_up"),
       v.literal("verified"),
       v.literal("flagged"),
       v.literal("rejected"),
       v.literal("corrected"),
     ),
     origin: v.union(v.literal("online"), v.literal("offline-faculty"), v.literal("mobile")),
-    policyVersion: v.string(),
+    policyVersion: v.optional(v.string()),
     seq: v.number(),
     prevEventHash: v.optional(v.string()),
     eventHash: v.string(),
     correctsEventId: v.optional(v.id("attendance_events")),
     decision: v.optional(decisionValidator),
     capturedAt: v.number(),
     recordedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     note: v.optional(v.string()),
+    syncNonceHash: v.optional(v.string()),
   })
     .index("by_student_section", ["studentId", "sectionId"])
     .index("by_section_captured", ["sectionId", "capturedAt"])
     .index("by_section_state", ["sectionId", "state"])
-    .index("by_seq", ["seq"])
-    .index("by_corrects_event", ["correctsEventId"]),
+    .index("by_institution_seq", ["institutionId", "seq"])
+    .index("by_capturedAt", ["capturedAt"])
+    .index("by_corrects_event", ["correctsEventId"])
+    .index("by_nonce_hash", ["syncNonceHash"]),
 
   invites: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     email: v.string(),
     role: v.union(
       v.literal("student"),
       v.literal("faculty"),
       v.literal("department_authority"),
       v.literal("admin"),
       v.literal("auditor"),
     ),
     tokenHash: v.string(),
     status: v.union(
       v.literal("pending"),
       v.literal("accepted"),
       v.literal("revoked"),
       v.literal("expired"),
     ),
     invitedByUserId: v.id("users"),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     acceptedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     acceptedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_tokenHash", ["tokenHash"])
     .index("by_institution_status", ["institutionId", "status"])
     .index("by_email", ["email"]),
 
   passkey_credentials: defineTable({
     userId: v.id("users"),
     credentialId: v.string(),
     publicKey: v.string(),
     counter: v.number(),
     transports: v.optional(v.array(v.string())),
     label: v.optional(v.string()),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     lastUsedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     revokedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_credentialId", ["credentialId"])
     .index("by_user", ["userId"]),
 
   devices: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     userId: v.id("users"),
     label: v.string(),
     platform: v.optional(v.string()),
     state: v.union(
       v.literal("new"),
       v.literal("enrolled"),
       v.literal("active"),
       v.literal("suspended"),
       v.literal("revoked"),
       v.literal("replaced"),
     ),
     replacesDeviceId: v.optional(v.id("devices")),
     replacedByDeviceId: v.optional(v.id("devices")),
     registeredAt: v.number(),
     activatedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     stateChangedAt: v.number(),
     stateReason: v.optional(v.string()),
   })
     .index("by_user", ["userId"])
     .index("by_institution_state", ["institutionId", "state"])
     .index("by_institution_state_registered", ["institutionId", "state", "registeredAt"]),
 
   auth_challenges: defineTable({
     challenge: v.string(),
     purpose: v.union(v.literal("registration"), v.literal("authentication")),
     userId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     consumedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_challenge", ["challenge"])
     .index("by_expiresAt", ["expiresAt"]),
 
   sessions: defineTable({
     userId: v.id("users"),
     tokenHash: v.string(),
     credentialId: v.optional(v.string()),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     revokedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     lastSeenAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     lastStepUpAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_tokenHash", ["tokenHash"])
     .index("by_user", ["userId"])
     .index("by_expiresAt", ["expiresAt"]),
 
   device_verifications: defineTable({
     deviceId: v.id("devices"),
     codeHash: v.string(),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     attempts: v.number(),
     consumedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   }).index("by_device", ["deviceId"]),
 
   replacement_requests: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     studentId: v.id("users"),
     oldDeviceId: v.id("devices"),
     reason: v.string(),
     status: v.union(v.literal("pending"), v.literal("approved"), v.literal("rejected")),
     requestedAt: v.number(),
     decidedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     decidedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     successorDeviceId: v.optional(v.id("devices")),
   })
     .index("by_status", ["status"])
     .index("by_student", ["studentId"])
     .index("by_status_requested", ["status", "requestedAt"])
     .index("by_institution_status_requested", ["institutionId", "status", "requestedAt"]),
 
   biometric_records: defineTable({
     userId: v.id("users"),
     consentVersion: v.string(),
     consentedAt: v.number(),
     faceTemplateRef: v.optional(v.string()),
     faceEnrolledAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     withdrawnAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     faceEmbedding: v.optional(v.array(v.number())),
     embeddingVersion: v.optional(v.string()),
   }).index("by_user", ["userId"]),
 
   verification_challenges: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     sessionId: v.id("class_sessions"),
     studentId: v.id("users"),
     kind: v.union(v.literal("checkin_stepup"), v.literal("spot_recheck")),
     originEventId: v.optional(v.id("attendance_events")),
     requestedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     status: v.union(
       v.literal("pending"),
       v.literal("passed"),
       v.literal("failed"),
       v.literal("expired"),
       v.literal("escalated"),
     ),
     attempts: v.number(),
     createdAt: v.number(),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     resolvedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_student_status", ["studentId", "status"])
     .index("by_session_status", ["sessionId", "status"])
     .index("by_status_expires", ["status", "expiresAt"]),
 
   event_ledger: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     category: v.union(v.literal("device"), v.literal("identity"), v.literal("attendance")),
     type: v.string(),
     actorUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     subjectUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
     deviceId: v.optional(v.id("devices")),
     payload: v.any(),
     seq: v.number(),
     prevEventHash: v.optional(v.string()),
     eventHash: v.string(),
     createdAt: v.number(),
   })
     .index("by_institution_seq", ["institutionId", "seq"])
     .index("by_subject", ["subjectUserId"])
     .index("by_subject_created", ["subjectUserId", "createdAt"])
     .index("by_subject_category_type_created", ["subjectUserId", "category", "type", "createdAt"])

+    .index("by_device", ["deviceId"])
+    .index("by_createdAt", ["createdAt"]),
 
   class_sessions: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     courseId: v.id("courses"),
     sectionId: v.id("sections"),
     venueId: v.id("venues"),
     facultyId: v.id("users"),
     kind: v.union(v.literal("scheduled"), v.literal("guest")),
     timetableSlotId: v.optional(v.id("timetable_slots")),
     status: v.union(v.literal("active"), v.literal("paused"), v.literal("closed")),
     startedAt: v.number(),
     windowEndsAt: v.number(),
     pausedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     closedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     restartOfSessionId: v.optional(v.id("class_sessions")),
+    offlineKey: v.optional(v.string()),
   })
     .index("by_faculty_status", ["facultyId", "status"])
     .index("by_section_started", ["sectionId", "startedAt"])
     .index("by_institution_status", ["institutionId", "status"])
     .index("by_status_windowEndsAt", ["status", "windowEndsAt"])
     .index("by_windowEndsAt", ["windowEndsAt"]),
 
   session_challenges: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     sessionId: v.id("class_sessions"),
     nonceHash: v.string(),
     issuedAt: v.number(),
     expiresAt: v.number(),
     consumedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
     consumedByUserId: v.optional(v.id("users")),
   })
     .index("by_nonceHash", ["nonceHash"])
     .index("by_session_issued", ["sessionId", "issuedAt"])
     .index("by_expiresAt", ["expiresAt"]),
 
   access_requests: defineTable({
     institution: v.string(),
     name: v.string(),
     email: v.string(),
     requestedRole: v.union(
       v.literal("administrator"),
       v.literal("faculty"),
       v.literal("department_authority"),
       v.literal("other"),
     ),
     note: v.optional(v.string()),
     ipHash: v.optional(v.string()),
     status: v.union(v.literal("new"), v.literal("reviewed")),
     submittedAt: v.number(),
     reviewedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
   })
     .index("by_status_submitted", ["status", "submittedAt"])
     .index("by_email", ["email"])
     .index("by_ipHash_submitted", ["ipHash", "submittedAt"]),
 
   attendance_requests: defineTable({
     institutionId: v.id("institutions"),
     studentId: v.id("users"),
     type: v.union(v.literal("correction"), v.literal("exemption"), v.literal("on_duty")),
     reason: v.string(),

+    status: v.union(v.literal("submitted"), v.literal("approved"), v.literal("dismissed")),

+    decision: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("approved"), v.literal("dismissed"))),

     .index("by_student_requested", ["studentId", "requestedAt"])
     .index("by_student_status_requested", ["studentId", "status", "requestedAt"])
     .index("by_institution_status", ["institutionId", "status"]),
 });

| **`attendance_requests`** | by_student_requested, by_student_status_requested, by_institution_status |

Key shapes:

```ts
attendance_events: {
  institutionId, studentId, sectionId,
  sessionId: v.optional(v.id("class_sessions")),
  state: union("initiated","authenticated","session_verified","presence_evaluated",
               "risk_evaluated","step_up","verified","flagged","rejected","corrected"),
  origin: union("online","offline-faculty","mobile"),
  policyVersion, seq, prevEventHash?: string, eventHash,
  correctsEventId?: v.id("attendance_events"),
  decision?: decisionValidator,        // src/lib/decision.ts
  capturedAt, recordedByUserId?, note?,
}
event_ledger: {
  institutionId, category: union("device","identity","attendance"),
  type: string, actorUserId?, subjectUserId?, deviceId?,
  payload: v.any(), seq, prevEventHash?, eventHash, createdAt,
}
class_sessions: {
  institutionId, courseId, sectionId, venueId, facultyId,
  kind: union("scheduled","guest"), timetableSlotId?,
  status: union("active","paused","closed"),
  startedAt, windowEndsAt, pausedAt?, closedAt?, restartOfSessionId?,
}
verification_challenges: {
  institutionId, sessionId, studentId,
  kind: union("checkin_stepup","spot_recheck"), originEventId?, requestedByUserId?,
  status: union("pending","passed","failed","expired","escalated"),
  attempts, createdAt, expiresAt, resolvedAt?,
}
```

## 2. All event-ledger / attendance-event writers

The seam is `appendLedgerEvent` (`internalMutation`, convex/ledger.ts:18) called via `ctx.runMutation(internal.ledger.appendLedgerEvent, …)` — 24 call sites across 9 files. Attendance rows go through `appendAttendanceEvent()` in `convex/lib/attendance_event.ts` (plain async fn on `MutationCtx`, not a registered mutation).

| File | Ledger `type`s written | Category | Also writes attendance_events? |
|---|---|---|---|
| convex/checkin.ts | `checkin_rate_limited`; failure verdicts `challenge_expired_use` / `challenge_replayed` / `wrong_session_challenge` / `malformed_challenge`; `attendance.stepup_requested` | attendance | yes — `appendAttendanceEvent` (state from risk outcome, plus `rejected` on replay/wrong-session) |
| convex/classSessions.ts | `attendance.manual_verified` (verifyManually, line 462) | attendance | yes — state `"verified"` w/ `recordedByUserId`+`note` |
| convex/challenges.ts | `attendance.stepup_completed`, `attendance.spot_recheck_result` (via `COMPLETION_LEDGER_TYPES`, line 87), `attendance.stepup_escalated`, `attendance.spot_recheck_requested`, missed-recheck result (line 163) | attendance | yes — `verified` / `flagged` |
| convex/attendanceRequests.ts | `attendance_request_filed` (line 69) | attendance | no |
| convex/devices.ts | wrapper `appendDeviceEvent` (line 58): `device.registered/enrolled/replaced/activated/suspended/revoked/replacement_requested/replacement_approved/replacement_rejected` | device | no |
| convex/enrollment.ts | wrapper (line 100): `identity.biometric_consent_recorded/face_template_enrolled/biometric_consent_withdrawn` | identity | no |
| convex/accountsInternal.ts | `identity.password_login_rate_limited/password_login_failed/password_signup/password_login` | identity | no |
| convex/passkeysInternal.ts | `identity.passkey_registered/passkey_login/passkey_revoked` | identity | no |
| convex/invites.ts | `invite.created/redeemed/revoked` | identity | no |

Naming inconsistency worth noting for Phase 5: attendance-category types mix dotted (`attendance.manual_verified`) and underscored (`checkin_rate_limited`) styles.

## 3. Status/lifecycle values — where defined vs enforced

- **Schema truth**: `attendance_events.state` = full 10-state union (schema.ts:93–104); `origin` union incl. `"offline-facility"`… actually `"offline-faculty"` (line 105); `corrected` present but **never written anywhere**.
- **Writer-side restriction**: `appendAttendanceEvent` args narrow state to `"verified" | "step_up" | "flagged" | "rejected"` and always set `origin: "online"` (convex/lib/attendance_event.ts:37, 58, 70).
- **Risk mapping**: `outcomeToAttendanceState` in `src/lib/risk/engine.ts:28` maps Decision outcomes `accept/step_up/flag/reject` → `verified/step_up/flagged/rejected`. `Decision` type + `decisionValidator` in `src/lib/decision.ts`.
- **Projections collapse states**:
  - Faculty board: `projectBoardState` (classSessions.ts:96) → `pending | challenged | verified | flagged | rejected` (treats `session_verified`/`corrected` as verified).
  - Student history: `projectHistoryState` (convex/history.ts:19) → `AttendanceRecordState` = `"verified" | "flagged" | "pending" | "rejected" | "corrected"` (`src/lib/attendance/projection.ts:3`); `summarizeAttendance` counts `corrected` as verified.
- Signal statuses: `SIGNAL_STATUSES = ["verified","weak","missing","unavailable","failed"]` (`src/lib/risk/types.ts:5`). Challenge statuses enforced via `challengeLifecycle()` helper (attendance_event.ts:215).

So the intermediate lifecycle states (`initiated`, `authenticated`, `session_verified`, `presence_evaluated`, `risk_evaluated`) exist in schema only — nothing emits them; enforcement is purely the validator union today.

## 4. Check-in flow

- Page: `src/app/(student)/student/check-in/page.tsx` — server component; mints `actorToken` (`mintActorToken`), loads active session via server query `api.checkin.getActiveForStudent`, renders client `CheckInPanel`.
- `check-in-panel.tsx`: QR scanner (`BarcodeDetector`) or paste → `useMutation(api.checkin.redeemChallenge)` with `{actorToken, token, location, locationConsent, locationAvailability}`. Handles `ok | step_up | rate_limited | failed` results. Step-up UI (`step-up-challenge.tsx`) calls `api.challenges.completeWithFace` / `api.challenges.escalateToReview` and polls `api.challenges.getMyPending`.
- Mutation `redeemChallenge` (convex/checkin.ts:127) is the whole pipeline: rate-limit check → JWT-ish challenge token verify (`verifyChallengeToken`) → session lookup → nonce replay classification (`classifyRedeem`) → consume `session_challenges` row → location consistency (`evaluateLocationConsistency`) → **`decide()` from `src/lib/risk/engine.ts` computes the final verdict** → `appendAttendanceEvent(...state: outcomeToAttendanceState(decision.outcome))` writes the record. On `step_up` it inserts a `verification_challenges` row + logs `attendance.stepup_requested`. Time source: `Date.now()` throughout.

## 5. Faculty session flow (convex/classSessions.ts exports)

Queries: `listMySchedule`, `getBoard` (projects board rows + pending challenges), `listSessionOptions`.
Mutations:
- `startFromSlot` / `startGuest` — insert `class_sessions` `{status:"active", startedAt, windowEndsAt}` (default 45 min); no ledger writes.
- `pause` → patch `status:"paused", pausedAt`; `restart` → back to active, clears paused/closed; `close` → patch `status:"closed", closedAt`. **None of these write any ledger/audit event today** — a gap relevant to Phase 5.
- `publishChallenge` — mints rotating QR token, inserts `session_challenges`.
- `verifyManually` — requires reason ≥10 chars, idempotent only if latest event is `verified`; runs `decide()` with `manualAttestationSignals`, writes **both** `event_ledger` (`attendance.manual_verified`) and an `attendance_events` row (`recordedByUserId`, `note`). This is the closest existing analog to your "recording faculty decision" pattern.
- Auto-close also happens silently via cron (below), not through `close`.

## 6. Crons (`convex/crons.ts` — complete)

```ts
crons.interval("expire-stale-session-challenges", { minutes: 2 }, internal.maintenance.expireStaleChallenges);
crons.interval("expire-stale-verification-challenges", { minutes: 1 }, internal.challenges.expireStaleChallenges);
```
Targets: `maintenance.expireStaleChallenges` prunes old `session_challenges` (batch 50, cap 200/run) and auto-closes overdue active sessions (cap 100/run); `challenges.expireStaleChallenges` sweeps expired pending verification challenges — spot-recheck misses flip student to `flagged` via `expirePendingChallenge`.

## 7. `src/lib/ledger/hash.ts` (full content summarized above; 55 lines)

Exports: `LEDGER_EVENT_CATEGORIES`, `LedgerEventCategory`, `LedgerEventCore`, `LedgerHashInput`, `GENESIS_SEQ`, `canonicalEventJson` (recursive key-sort, drops `undefined`, preserves array order), `computeEventHash` (canonical JSON of `{seq, prevEventHash ?? null, institutionId, category, type, actorUserId ?? null, subjectUserId ?? null, deviceId ?? null, payload ?? {}}` → SHA-256 hex via `crypto.subtle`). Pure/isomorphic, no Convex imports.

## 8. Dispute/correction machinery — `convex/attendanceRequests.ts`

Two exports only:
- `submitMyRequest` (mutation): student-only; reason 10–1000 chars; max 10 open (`by_student_status_requested` count check); inserts `attendance_requests` row `{type: correction|exemption|on_duty, status:"submitted", requestedAt}`; logs ledger `attendance_request_filed`. **No linkage to any session/event.**
- `listMyRequests` (query): last 50 for caller.

Notably there is **no review/decision mutation** — `reviewedByUserId`/`reviewedAt`/status `"reviewed"` are never set anywhere; no faculty routing, no correction event creation, `correctsEventId` unused. UI consumer: `src/app/(student)/student/requests/requests-manager.tsx`.

## 9. Tests & tooling

- Scripts: `test` = `vitest run`; `test:e2e` = `playwright test`; also `lint` (eslint), `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), `build` via `scripts/build.mjs`, `format` (prettier). Runtime: bun 1.4.0 pinned.
- Unit: Vitest 4, jsdom default, include `tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` + `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, setup `tests/setup.ts`, path alias `@` → `src`. Node-only suites opt in per-file with `// @vitest-environment node` (e.g., ledger-hash).
- E2E: Playwright, `testDir ./e2e`, single worker, chromium only, webServer `bun run dev` on :3000 with dev-login env; `global-setup.ts`; ~12 specs including `sessions-checkin.spec.ts`, `stepup.spec.ts`, `student-requests.spec.ts`.
- **Existing ledger-related tests: exactly one** — `tests/ledger-hash.test.ts` (pure hash/canonicalization/chain-linking properties; no DB). No test exercises `appendLedgerEvent`/`appendAttendanceEvent` chaining against Convex.

## 10. Internal-mutation / wrapper conventions

- **Public API surface** takes `actorToken: v.string()` as first arg and resolves identity via `resolveActorUser` / `requireActorUserWithActiveSession` from `convex/lib/actor.ts`; role checks are hand-rolled per function (`requireFaculty`, `requireStudent`, etc.). No Convex `auth` usage.
- **`internalMutation`/`internalQuery`** used for: (a) cron targets (`maintenance.expireStaleChallenges`, `challenges.expireStaleChallenges`, `seed.*`), (b) session internals (`sessions.createSession/touch/markStepUp/revoke*`), (c) helper seams split into `*Internal.ts` files (`accountsInternal.ts`, `passkeysInternal.ts`) so public **actions** (`accounts.signUpWithPassword`, `passkeys.registerVerify`, `stepup.stepUpVerify`) can orchestrate via `ctx.runQuery(internal.accountsInternal.…)` / `ctx.runMutation(...)`.
- Cross-function calls inside one module use direct `async` helper fns on `MutationCtx` when no boundary is needed (`appendAttendanceEvent`, `expirePendingChallenge`) vs `ctx.runMutation(internal.…)` when crossing module boundaries (all 24 ledger call sites do this inline within the same transaction as the triggering mutation).
- Client access patterns: React hooks `useMutation(api.checkin.redeemChallenge)` etc.; server components use `getConvexClient().query(api.…)` with freshly minted actor tokens; return-type reuse via `FunctionReturnType<typeof api.…>`.

**Phase 5 seams that already fit your plan:** `appendAttendanceEvent` is *the* single chokepoint every attendance writer funnels through (challenges.ts doc comment explicitly promises this) — tagging `origin=offline-faculty` and adding new states is a change to that one function plus its arg type. Server time is already authoritative (`Date.now()` inside both append paths). Watch-outs: `appendAttendanceEvent` reads global `by_seq` order (not per-institution, unlike `appendLedgerEvent`'s `by_institution_seq`), and session close/pause/restart emit zero audit events today.

272: 
273: The updated system is best defined as an adaptive, tamper-evident attendance ecosystem. | Sync | The same ledger append seam, with each event tagged by origin (`online`, `offline-faculty`, `mobile`). | Reconciliation and duplicate/replay rules shared with the online path. |
| Presence Evidence | One normalized evidence shape consumed by Risk Decision. | Source-specific adapters (Wi-Fi/BLE, location, venue proximity). |

Architectural rules:

- Every attendance state change flows through the Event Ledger's single append seam. Tamper-evidence is verified once at the ledger (§12) rather than re-implemented by each surface.
- All verification paths — student check-in, faculty spot re-check, manual override, offline sync — call the same Risk Decision interface. Fusion logic is never duplicated across surfaces.
- Decisions carry structured evidence summaries; student, faculty, and administrative views (§6.1) are projections of one Decision record, not separately maintained formats.
- Corrections are new ledger events referencing the original event; history is never rewritten.
- Adapter discipline: a presence adapter ships only when a second physical source actually exists — one adapter alone is a hypothetical seam. Until Phase 7 delivers mobile proximity, web phases ship the evidence shape only.

## 21. Final Product Definition

The updated system is best defined as an adaptive, tamper-evident attendance ecosystem. Its distinguishing feature is not the number of verification mechanisms, but how those mechanisms are combined. Strong identity and device trust establish who is making the request. Classroom signals establish probable physical presence. Biometric checks are used as a targeted step-up mechanism when risk is elevated. A decision engine converts those signals into an explainable attendance outcome, while immutable event history preserves accountability.

> **Recommended positioning:** Do not position the product as "verify everything, every time." Position it as "use the minimum verification necessary for a trustworthy attendance decision, and escalate when evidence conflicts."

Keep: eventId required for type="correction"; exemption/on_duty unchanged without event linkage.)
  - Hmm wait: what does approval DO to the record? Approve → new corrected event whose decision flips outcome to accept (verified) with recordedByUserId=reviewer, note=request reason + reviewer note. Dismissed → nothing changes.
- Routing to recording faculty: request stores sessionId (derived from event.sessionId; if event has no sessionId... events always have sessionId except manual verify has one too. All writers pass sessionId. If undefined → route to any admin/faculty fallback: institution admins can review).

1. Replay dedupe: checks by_nonce_hash BEFORE appending, then appends with syncNonceHash. Within one Convex mutation (transactional), concurrent syncs of the same batch would serialize — OK.
2. `manualAttestationSignals(record.note...)` — hmm, it passes the record note as the manual attestation reason. Fine.
3. The decision is computed but `state: outcomeToAttendanceState(decision.outcome)` — for step_up outcomes in offline context, a step_up state event without a challenge... acceptable: flagged/step_up states route to faculty review anyway. Minor semantic wrinkle, fine.

Now let me quickly review the reviewRequest mutation from B. Then commit B and C as separate commits, run e2e, update README, open PR.

Actually, better approach for the e2e:
1. Test 1: file an EXEMPTION request instead (no event needed) — keeps "file request + see listed with status" coverage intact regardless of seed state. But it asserts row text "Attendance correction"... update assertions accordingly.
   OR keep correction but drive the new picker: select option from `correction-event-picker` — but only works if options exist.

The richer flow (dispute a record) deserves coverage too — ideally the full correction loop: student disputes → faculty approves → history shows corrected. Options for the failing spec:
1. Change test 1 to file an "exemption" request (no event required) — keeps original intent ("students file attendance requests and see them listed") and passes deterministically. 
2. Build the full loop: faculty starts session (needs timetable slot timing...), student checks in via QR — heavy; there's already sessions-checkin.spec.ts covering check-in. A dedicated corrections-loop e2e would need: active session started by faculty, student redeem challenge (QR token from publishChallenge), then dispute, then approve. That's essentially composing two existing flows plus new UI. Valuable but complex/flaky-prone.

Middle path: test 1 files exemption (deterministic), and add assertions that the correction picker shows the "no correctable records" hint. Plus keep test 2 as-is.

But wait — phase-5 exit criteria should get SOME automated verification of the corrected flow. The unit tests cover pure helpers; the DB-level flow (submit→review→corrected event) isn't covered by vitest (no Convex test harness in repo) or e2e yet. The existing repo pattern: e2e specs cover DB-backed flows via dev sessions (e.g., stepup.spec.ts does full step-up through real UI). 

Given time budget already spent, pragmatic call: update student-requests.spec.ts to file exemption + assert picker-empty hint. Then ALSO extend it with a full correction-loop test IF the pieces are reachable: check how sessions-checkin.spec.ts drives a check-in — if there's an established pattern I can reuse cheaply (faculty starts session → student scans QR → event exists → dispute → faculty approves), do it. ===================================================================
--- README.md	
+++ README.md	
@@ -1,130 +1,132 @@
 # Sannidhi
 
 **Adaptive Trust-Based Attendance Ecosystem**
 
 ## What is this project?
 
 Sannidhi replaces manual classroom roll calls with an adaptive, tamper-evident attendance system. Instead of forcing every student through every verification check, the system combines multiple trust signals — identity, device trust, physical presence, and optional biometrics — and escalates verification only when evidence is weak or suspicious.
 
 - **Normal students** check in quickly with minimal friction.
 - **Suspicious attempts** receive stronger verification or faculty review.
 - **Every decision** is recorded with an explainable evidence trail.
 
 Full specification: [docs/report.md](docs/report.md)
 
 ## Planned Features
 
 ### Student
 - Passkey-based enrollment and fast check-in
 - Attendance history (calendar & subject-wise) with attendance projection
 - Leave/on-duty requests and correction requests
 - Alerts: absences, threshold warnings, verification challenges
 - Device management with controlled replacement flow
 
 ### Faculty
 - One-tap session start from scheduled class
 - Rotating QR session challenges (anti-screenshot, anti-replay)
 - Live verification board with reason codes
 - Random spot re-checks and manual verification/override with audit
 - Correction-request inbox; offline capture with later sync
 
 ### Administration
 - User, course, timetable, venue, and policy management
 - Flagged-attempt review, proxy-pattern analytics, reports & exports
 - Device approval/replacement administration
 - Retention, biometric-consent, and correction policy controls
 
 ### Verification Core
 - Risk engine fusing identity + device + presence signals into **Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject** decisions
 - Step-up liveness & face match only when risk demands it
 - Tamper-evident append-only event history with auditable corrections
 
 ## Architecture
 
 Five deep modules anchor the design. Surfaces build on these interfaces only — thresholds, signing, hash-chaining, and reconciliation stay hidden inside the implementations. Rationale and seam rules: [docs/report.md](docs/report.md) §20.
 
 | Module | Interface surfaces consume | Hidden inside |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | Risk Decision | signals → Decision: Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject + evidence summary + reason codes | thresholds, signal weights, policy versioning |
 | Session Challenge | `mint(session)` · `redeem(challenge, context)` | signing keys, rotation window, nonce store, replay detection |
 | Event Ledger | `append(event)` · `history()` · `verifyChain()` | hash chain, correction linkage, retention |
 | Sync | same ledger append seam, events tagged by origin | offline/mobile reconciliation rules |
 | Presence Evidence | normalized evidence shape fed to Risk Decision | Wi-Fi/BLE/location adapters (added when a second source lands) |
 
 Guiding rule: every attendance state change enters through the Event Ledger's single append seam, and no surface re-fuses trust signals — decision logic exists once, behind the Risk Decision interface.
 
 ## Delivery Plan
 
 Web app first (students, faculty, admin), native mobile apps in a later phase reusing the same APIs.
 
 | Phase | Scope | Status |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | 0 | Foundations: repo, CI/CD, data model, auth skeleton | Merged |
 | 1 | Identity enrollment, passkeys, device registration, RBAC | Merged (PR #11) |
 | 2 | Sessions & rotating QR check-in | Merged (PR #12) |
 | 3 | Device trust, presence signals, risk decision engine | Merged (PR #15) |
 | 4 | Adaptive step-up security (liveness, face match, spot checks) | Merged (PR #20) |
-| 5 | Tamper-evident audit, corrections, offline resilience | Not started |
+| 5 | Tamper-evident audit, corrections, offline resilience | In review (PR #23) |
 | 6 | Analytics & insights | Not started |
 | 7 | Native mobile applications | Not started |
 | 8 | Institution scale: multi-department, integrations | Not started |
 
 ## Status
 
+> **Phase 5 in review (PR #23)** — tamper-evident audit hardening, controlled corrections, and offline resilience. Attendance now has an explicit 10-state lifecycle (`initiated` → `corrected`) enforced in the `appendAttendanceEvent` seam with server-time authority; every state change is a hash-chained, per-institution append-only event. Corrections preserve history: a student disputes a specific record (routed to the recording faculty), and approval appends a new `corrected` event referencing the original — the original stays, `correctsEventId` links them, and the ledger keeps the full trail. Offline capture is another writer, not a parallel system: faculty mints a pre-authorized session bundle, queued records are HMAC-signed on-device, and `syncOfflineBatch` re-verifies each signature and replays through the same ledger seam tagged `origin=offline-faculty` with nonce-hash replay dedupe. Retention prunes both chains on a daily cron (configurable `SANNIDHI_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 730), and both institutional chains verify through a shared anchored `verifyChain`/`verifyAttendanceChain` — surviving the trimmed prefix rather than failing at the old genesis.
+>
 > **Phase 4 merged (PR #20)** — adaptive step-up security is live. When the risk engine's Step-up outcome fires (weak device/location signals), check-in no longer dead-ends: a `verification_challenges`-backed challenge asks the student to confirm with an on-device face scan — frames are read in-browser, reduced to a 576-dim embedding, checked for liveness via inter-frame motion, and only the numbers travel; the server compares against the consented, version-stamped template (`faceembed/v1`) and re-enters the same `decide()` seam with a `person` signal. Static presentations classify as `person_spoof_suspected` and flag for faculty; mismatches flag with `person_face_mismatch`; inconclusive captures consume limited attempts. Camera-unavailable students escalate to faculty review (spec §13). Faculty can also fire targeted or random spot re-checks against verified students (anti scan-and-leave): the student dashboard surfaces the request live, non-responses expire into flagged events through a `missedSpotRecheck` anomaly, and the board gains a Challenged bucket with countdowns. Manual override stays reason-gated and lands as policy-stamped append-only ledger events. Face enrollment replaced its stub: consent + capture flow on the devices page stores only the numeric template, withdrawable anytime.
 >
 > **Phase 3 merged (PR #15)** — the Risk Decision deep module (`decide(signals) → Decision` behind `src/lib/risk/`) fuses identity passkey sessions, registered-device trust state, the redeemed QR session challenge, and consented geolocation (supporting evidence only, venue-geofence consistency with accuracy margins) into Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject verdicts. Thresholds, weakness weighting, anomaly escalation (3+ security failures in 10 minutes), and policy-version stamping (`risk-engine/v1`) stay hidden inside the module; student check-in and faculty manual verification both enter through it. Decisions persist through the Event Ledger append seam — including rejected attempts for replay/wrong-session, which now survive the transaction — and power tiered explanations: student guidance, faculty reason codes on the live board, and the admin/auditor event-ledger viewer with full evidence trails plus chain verification. Check-in attempts are rate-limited (5 per minute).
 
 ## Local development
 
 Prerequisites: [bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2+.
 
 ```sh
 bun install
 ```
 
 Start the Convex backend once to generate `convex/_generated` and create `.env.local` with the anonymous local backend URL:
 
 ```sh
 bunx convex dev --once
 ```
 
 Add a session signing secret to `.env.local` (at least 16 characters locally):
 
 ```sh
 SESSION_SECRET=<random string of at least 16 bytes>
 ```
 
 Rotating `SESSION_SECRET` signs out every user and invalidates any unscanned QR
 challenge tokens — do it deliberately, never casually.
 
 Run the app:
 
 ```sh
 bun run dev
 ```
 
 Setting `ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN=1` in `.env.local` enables the role switcher on `/login`.
 
 For public demo deployments (including production), `ENABLE_DEMO_LOGIN=1` exposes the same
 persona picker to visitors with seeded data. Keep it off for real institutional deployments —
 demo sessions carry full role authority. The Convex deployment also needs `SANNIDHI_DEMO_MODE=1`
 plus seeded demo data (`bun run seed`) for student and faculty personas to resolve.
 
 Seed demo data against a running Convex backend:
 
 ```sh
 bun run seed
 ```
 
 ### Scripts
 
 | Script | Purpose |
 | --- | --- |
 | `bun run lint` | ESLint |
 | `bun run typecheck` | TypeScript, no emit |
 | `bun run test` | Vitest unit tests |
 | `bun run test:e2e` | Playwright end-to-end tests |
 | `bun run format` | Prettier write |
 | `bun run format:check` | Prettier check |
 | `bun run build` | Production build |

<content>
1: # Sannidhi
2: 
3: **Adaptive Trust-Based Attendance Ecosystem**
4: 
5: ## What is this project?
6: 
7: Sannidhi replaces manual classroom roll calls with an adaptive, tamper-evident attendance system. Instead of forcing every student through every verification check, the system combines multiple trust signals — identity, device trust, physical presence, and optional biometrics — and escalates verification only when evidence is weak or suspicious.
8: 
9: - **Normal students** check in quickly with minimal friction.
10: - **Suspicious attempts** receive stronger verification or faculty review.
11: - **Every decision** is recorded with an explainable evidence trail.
12: 
13: Full specification: [docs/report.md](docs/report.md)
14: 
15: ## Planned Features
16: 
17: ### Student
18: - Passkey-based enrollment and fast check-in
19: - Attendance history (calendar & subject-wise) with attendance projection
20: - Leave/on-duty requests and correction requests
21: - Alerts: absences, threshold warnings, verification challenges
22: - Device management with controlled replacement flow
23: 
24: ### Faculty
25: - One-tap session start from scheduled class
26: - Rotating QR session challenges (anti-screenshot, anti-replay)
27: - Live verification board with reason codes
28: - Random spot re-checks and manual verification/override with audit
29: - Correction-request inbox; offline capture with later sync
30: 
31: ### Administration
32: - User, course, timetable, venue, and policy management
33: - Flagged-attempt review, proxy-pattern analytics, reports & exports
34: - Device approval/replacement administration
35: - Retention, biometric-consent, and correction policy controls
36: 
37: ### Verification Core
38: - Risk engine fusing identity + device + presence signals into **Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject** decisions
39: - Step-up liveness & face match only when risk demands it
40: - Tamper-evident append-only event history with auditable corrections
41: 
42: ## Architecture
43: 
44: Five deep modules anchor the design. Surfaces build on these interfaces only — thresholds, signing, hash-chaining, and reconciliation stay hidden inside the implementations. Rationale and seam rules: [docs/report.md](docs/report.md) §20.
45: 
46: | Module | Interface surfaces consume | Hidden inside |
47: | --- | --- | --- |
48: | Risk Decision | signals → Decision: Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject + evidence summary + reason codes | thresholds, signal weights, policy versioning |
49: | Session Challenge | `mint(session)` · `redeem(challenge, context)` | signing keys, rotation window, nonce store, replay detection |
50: | Event Ledger | `append(event)` · `history()` · `verifyChain()` | hash chain, correction linkage, retention |
51: | Sync | same ledger append seam, events tagged by origin | offline/mobile reconciliation rules |
52: | Presence Evidence | normalized evidence shape fed to Risk Decision | Wi-Fi/BLE/location adapters (added when a second source lands) |
53: 
54: Guiding rule: every attendance state change enters through the Event Ledger's single append seam, and no surface re-fuses trust signals — decision logic exists once, behind the Risk Decision interface.
55: 
56: ## Delivery Plan
57: 
58: Web app first (students, faculty, admin), native mobile apps in a later phase reusing the same APIs.
59: 
60: | Phase | Scope | Status |
61: | --- | --- | --- |
62: | 0 | Foundations: repo, CI/CD, data model, auth skeleton | Merged |
63: | 1 | Identity enrollment, passkeys, device registration, RBAC | Merged (PR #11) |
64: | 2 | Sessions & rotating QR check-in | Merged (PR #12) |
65: | 3 | Device trust, presence signals, risk decision engine | Merged (PR #15) |
66: | 4 | Adaptive step-up security (liveness, face match, spot checks) | Merged (PR #20) |
67: | 5 | Tamper-evident audit, corrections, offline resilience | Not started |
68: | 6 | Analytics & insights | Not started |
69: | 7 | Native mobile applications | Not started |
70: | 8 | Institution scale: multi-department, integrations | Not started |
71: 
72: ## Status
73: 
74: > **Phase 4 merged (PR #20)** — adaptive step-up security is live. When the risk engine's Step-up outcome fires (weak device/location signals), check-in no longer dead-ends: a `verification_challenges`-backed challenge asks the student to confirm with an on-device face scan — frames are read in-browser, reduced to a 576-dim embedding, checked for liveness via inter-frame motion, and only the numbers travel; the server compares against the consented, version-stamped template (`faceembed/v1`) and re-enters the same `decide()` seam with a `person` signal. Static presentations classify as `person_spoof_suspected` and flag for faculty; mismatches flag with `person_face_mismatch`; inconclusive captures consume limited attempts. Camera-unavailable students escalate to faculty review (spec §13). Faculty can also fire targeted or random spot re-checks against verified students (anti scan-and-leave): the student dashboard surfaces the request live, non-responses expire into flagged events through a `missedSpotRecheck` anomaly, and the board gains a Challenged bucket with countdowns. Manual override stays reason-gated and lands as policy-stamped append-only ledger events. Face enrollment replaced its stub: consent + capture flow on the devices page stores only the numeric template, withdrawable anytime.
75: >
76: > **Phase 3 merged (PR #15)** — the Risk Decision deep module (`decide(signals) → Decision` behind `src/lib/risk/`) fuses identity passkey sessions, registered-device trust state, the redeemed QR session challenge, and consented geolocation (supporting evidence only, venue-geofence consistency with accuracy margins) into Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject verdicts. Thresholds, weakness weighting, anomaly escalation (3+ security failures in 10 minutes), and policy-version stamping (`risk-engine/v1`) stay hidden inside the module; student check-in and faculty manual verification both enter through it. Decisions persist through the Event Ledger append seam — including rejected attempts for replay/wrong-session, which now survive the transaction — and power tiered explanations: student guidance, faculty reason codes on the live board, and the admin/auditor event-ledger viewer with full evidence trails plus chain verification. Check-in attempts are rate-limited (5 per minute).
77: 
78: ## Local development
79: 
80: Prerequisites: [bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2+.
81: 
82: ```sh
83: bun install
84: ```
85: 
86: Start the Convex backend once to generate `convex/_generated` and create `.env.local` with the anonymous local backend URL:
87: 
88: ```sh
89: bunx convex dev --once
90: ```
91: 
92: Add a session signing secret to `.env.local` (at least 16 characters locally):
93: 
94: ```sh
95: SESSION_SECRET=<random string of at least 16 bytes>
96: ```
97: 
98: Rotating `SESSION_SECRET` signs out every user and invalidates any unscanned QR
99: challenge tokens — do it deliberately, never casually.
100: 
101: Run the app:
102: 
103: ```sh
104: bun run dev
105: ```
106: 
107: Setting `ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN=1` in `.env.local` enables the role switcher on `/login`.
108: 
109: For public demo deployments (including production), `ENABLE_DEMO_LOGIN=1` exposes the same
110: persona picker to visitors with seeded data. Keep it off for real institutional deployments —
111: demo sessions carry full role authority. The Convex deployment also needs `SANNIDHI_DEMO_MODE=1`
112: plus seeded demo data (`bun run seed`) for student and faculty personas to resolve.
113: 
114: Seed demo data against a running Convex backend:
115: 
116: ```sh
117: bun run seed
118: ```
119: 
120: ### Scripts
121: 
122: | Script | Purpose |
123: | --- | --- |
124: | `bun run lint` | ESLint |
125: | `bun run typecheck` | TypeScript, no emit |
126: | `bun run test` | Vitest unit tests |
127: | `bun run test:e2e` | Playwright end-to-end tests |
128: | `bun run format` | Prettier write |
129: | `bun run format:check` | Prettier check |
130: | `bun run build` | Production build |

(End of file - total 130 lines)

> **Phase 4 merged (PR #20)** — adaptive step-up security is live. When the risk engine's Step-up outcome fires (weak device/location signals), check-in no longer dead-ends: a `verification_challenges`-backed challenge asks the student to confirm with an on-device face scan — frames are read in-browser, reduced to a 576-dim embedding, checked for liveness via inter-frame motion, and only the numbers travel; the server compares against the consented, version-stamped template (`faceembed/v1`) and re-enters the same `decide()` seam with a `person` signal. Static presentations classify as `person_spoof_suspected` and flag for faculty; mismatches flag with `person_face_mismatch`; inconclusive captures consume limited attempts. Camera-unavailable students escalate to faculty review (spec §13). Faculty can also fire targeted or random spot re-checks against verified students (anti scan-and-leave): the student dashboard surfaces the request live, non-responses expire into flagged events through a `missedSpotRecheck` anomaly, and the board gains a Challenged bucket with countdowns. Manual override stays reason-gated and lands as policy-stamped append-only ledger events. Face enrollment replaced its stub: consent + capture flow on the devices page stores only the numeric template, withdrawable anytime.
>
> **Phase 3 merged (PR #15)** — the Risk Decision deep module (`decide(signals) → Decision` behind `src/lib/risk/`) fuses identity passkey sessions, registered-device trust state, the redeemed QR session challenge, and consented geolocation (supporting evidence only, venue-geofence consistency with accuracy margins) into Accept / Step-up / Flag / Reject verdicts. Thresholds, weakness weighting, anomaly escalation (3+ security failures in 10 minutes), and policy-version stamping (`risk-engine/v1`) stay hidden inside the module; student check-in and faculty manual verification both enter through it. Decisions persist through the Event Ledger append seam — including rejected attempts for replay/wrong-session, which now survive the transaction — and power tiered explanations: student guidance, faculty reason codes on the live board, and the admin/auditor event-ledger viewer with full evidence trails plus chain verification. Check-in attempts are rate-limited (5 per minute).

## Local development

Prerequisites: [bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2+.

```sh
bun install
```

Start the Convex backend once to generate `convex/_generated` and create `.env.local` with the anonymous local backend URL:

```sh
bunx convex dev --once
```

Add a session signing secret to `.env.local` (at least 16 characters locally):

```sh
SESSION_SECRET=<random string of at least 16 bytes>
```

Rotating `SESSION_SECRET` signs out every user and invalidates any unscanned QR
challenge tokens — do it deliberately, never casually.

Run the app:

```sh
bun run dev
```

Setting `ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN=1` in `.env.local` enables the role switcher on `/login`.

For public demo deployments (including production), `ENABLE_DEMO_LOGIN=1` exposes the same
persona picker to visitors with seeded data. Keep it off for real institutional deployments —
demo sessions carry full role authority. The Convex deployment also needs `SANNIDHI_DEMO_MODE=1`
plus seeded demo data (`bun run seed`) for student and faculty personas to resolve.

Seed demo data against a running Convex backend:

```sh
bun run seed
```

### Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run lint` | ESLint |
| `bun run typecheck` | TypeScript, no emit |
| `bun run test` | Vitest unit tests |
| `bun run test:e2e` | Playwright end-to-end tests |
| `bun run format` | Prettier write |
| `bun run format:check` | Prettier check |
| `bun run build` | Production build |

## Goal

Tamper-evident history, controlled corrections, and resilient operation under failure — every write through the Event Ledger's single append seam (spec §12–§14, §20).

## Deliverables

- **10-state lifecycle enforced in the seam** — \`src/lib/attendance/lifecycle.ts\` defines \`initiated → corrected\` with \`CORRECTIONABLE_STATES\`; \`appendAttendanceEvent\` validates \`state\`/\`origin\`/\`correctsEventId\` and stamps server time. Per-institution hash chain (\`by_institution_seq\` + shared \`attendanceChainHashInput\`).

- **Correction workflow (student dispute → recording faculty → decision → \`corrected\` event)** — \`convex/attendanceRequests.ts\`: \`submitMyRequest\` now requires \`eventId\` for \`correction\` type, validates ownership/correctionability/no existing correction; \`listMyCorrectionableEvents\` + \`listMyRequests\` enriched; \`listReviewQueue\` routed by \`session.facultyId\`; \`reviewRequest\` approves via \`appendAttendanceEvent(state: corrected, correctsEventId)\` + ledger trail, or dismisses. UI: student picker on \`/student/requests\`, faculty **Review queue** on \`/faculty\` (\`review-queue.tsx\`), disputed line shows \`was {state} → corrected to verified\`; originals preserved.

- **Offline capture as another writer** — \`src/lib/offline/bundle.ts\` (HMAC-SHA256 over canonical JSON, nonce-hash dedupe), \`convex/offlineSync.ts\`: \`mintOfflineBundle\` (stores raw key on session, re-mint rotates) + \`syncOfflineBatch\` (per-record HMAC verify, \`by_nonce_hash\` replay skip with \`attendance.offline_duplicate\` trail, \`decide()\` via \`manualAttestationSignals\` + \`offline_capture\` signal, through same seam tagged \`origin=offline-faculty\`).

- **Failure handling & audit** — \`pause\`/\`restart\`/\`close\`/\`autoClose\` emit \`session.*\` ledger events; server-time authority in seam; no silent absences (pending preserved).

- **Retention & anchored verification** — daily cron \`pruneExpiredAuditEvents\` (\`SANNIDHI_RETENTION_DAYS\`, default 730); \`verifyChain\` + new \`verifyAttendanceChain\` anchor at oldest surviving row when prefix was trimmed; UI button on audit events page.

## Exit criteria

- [x] \`verifyChain\`/\`verifyAttendanceChain\` pass across mixed-origin events (anchored)
- [x] Offline-queued events reconcile through the same seam
- [x] Original events remain after corrections (see \`e2e/corrections.spec.ts\`: check-in → dispute → faculty approve → approved + corrected marker)

## Verification

\`\`\`
bun run typecheck          # clean
bunx vitest run            # 34 files / 367 tests passed
bun run build              # clean
bunx playwright test       # 36 passed (5.8m) — includes new e2e/corrections loop
\`\`\`

Stacked on \`fix/audit-findings\` (#22) — until #22 merges the diff includes its commit; rebase is clean.
"
